The Hon'ble Supreme Court has held in Pranay Sethi (supra):
"59.4 In case the deceased was self-employed or on a fixed salary, an addition of 40%
of the established income should be the warrant where the deceased was below the age of 40 years.
An addition of 25% where the deceased was between the age of 40 to 50 years and 10% where the deceased was between the age of 50 to 60 years should be regarded as the necessary method of computation.
The established income means the income minus the tax component."

The computation of just compensation is to be made in accordance with the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Sarla Verma and Others vs. DTC (2009)
6 SCC 121 which was affirmed by the Constitution Bench of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in National Insurance Company Limited vs. Pranay Sethi and Others (2017) 16 SCC 680.
Loss of Dependency 24.
As per the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Sarla Verma (supra)
and affirmed in Pranav Sethi (supra), three facts need to be established by the petitioners for assessing compensation in the case of death under the head of "Loss of Dependency" which are (a) age of the deceased (b) income of the deceased and (c) the number of dependents.
Age of the deceased 25.
As per the Aadhaar card of the deceased, his date of birth is 01.01.1997.
Accordingly, the deceased was aged 23 years at the time of the accident dated 24.11.2020.
25.1 Since the age of deceased falls in the age bracket of 21-25, therefore, as per Pranay Sethi (supra)
the multiplier of 18 is applicable in calculating the loss MACT No. 77/2021 Ravina & Ors.
The testimony of PW3, in the absence of supporting records such as attendance register,
salary register, or appointment letter of the deceased, does not inspire confidence.
Further, the contents of the FIR, wherein it is stated that the deceased was working in Gurugram, as well as the Registration Certificate of the JCB, also indicate that the deceased was not working in Delhi.
30.4 As per his Aadhaar card, the deceased was a resident of Haryana.
Since the petitioners have failed to prove his income, the same is to be assessed in accordance with the Minimum Wages Act, 1948, as applicable in Haryana.
The established income means the income minus the tax component."
